applicability: any repository developed on Windows whose CI runs POSIX, where a path test can pass vacuously on one platform

evidence.environment: ubuntu-latest CI vs Windows local development
evidence.source_reference: GitHub Actions run 31664718034, validate (ubuntu-latest, python3), PR #125

expected_behavior: A test asserting two spellings name the same file must prove that equality before exercising the guard, and path-equivalence fixtures must be constructed with os.path.join rather than string concatenation with a leading './'.
observation: A path-equivalence test built its second spelling as f"./{absolute_path}". On POSIX that yields a relative path to a nonexistent directory rather than an equivalent path, so the assertion was vacuous on Windows (where it happened to resolve equal) and failed on Linux. Five static review rounds and 818 local tests did not catch it; the first CI run did, in 75 seconds.

scope: tests that assert path equivalence or path-collision refusal

sensitivity_review.statement: Operator attested that the candidate contains no raw transcripts, secrets, credentials, or executable instructions.
